case_title: Vijay Singh @ Vijay Kr. Sharma v. The State of Bihar
trial_court_outcome: Accused nos. 1-5 convicted of offences u/ss. 302/34 and 364/34; accused nos. 6 and 7 acquitted of all charges
neutral_facts: The prosecution alleged that the deceased was abducted and murdered by seven accused persons during a property dispute. The accused persons were alleged to have taken the deceased from her father's house, where she was residing with her husband and brother-in-law. The accused were charged with offences under Sections 302, 364, and 34 of the Indian Penal Code. The trial court acquitted two accused persons, while convicting the remaining five. The High Court reversed the acquittal of the two accused persons, but the Supreme Court found the prosecution's case based on circumstantial evidence insufficient to meet the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt. The Supreme Court acquitted all seven accused persons, noting that the chain of evidence was incomplete and the prosecution failed to establish a direct link between the accused and the alleged offences.
